                        <div class="eche-officer-question">Your institution has established formal procedures for recognising staff mobility for both teaching and training activities abroad</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Ensuring that the mobile participant, sending and receiving institution/organisation/enterprise (i.e. all three parties) sign the mobility agreement before the start of the mobility</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>To ensure effective staff mobility, it has to be based on a signed mobility agreement. The mobility agreement has to acceptable and signed by all parties in advance. There are four key elements set out by the mobility agreement, which are intended to increase the relevance and potential impact of the mobility. These are:</p><ul><li>The overall objectives and academic rationale of the mobility,</li><li>The institutional requirements or strategy, and the mobility's added value in the context of modernisation and internationalisation,</li><li>The activities or teaching programme content to be undertaken by the staff member, and,</li><li>The expected outcomes and impact of the mobility on the professional development of the staff member at both institutions.</li></ul><p>For this to work effectively, there needs to be dialogue and discussion between the three parties prior to the signing of the mobility agreement having agreed the common goals which are acceptable.&nbsp;</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Ensuring that the mobile participant, sending and receiving institution/organisation/enterprise (i.e. all three parties) sign the mobility agreement before the start of the mobility</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>To ensure effective staff mobility, it has to be based on a signed mobility agreement. The mobility agreement has to acceptable and signed by all parties in advance. There are four key elements set out by the mobility agreement, which are intended to increase the relevance and potential impact of the mobility. These are:</p><ul><li>The overall objectives and academic rationale of the mobility,</li><li>The institutional requirements or strategy, and the mobility's added value in the context of modernisation and internationalisation,</li><li>The activities or teaching programme content to be undertaken by the staff member, and,</li><li>The expected outcomes and impact of the mobility on the professional development of the staff member at both institutions.</li></ul><p>For this to work effectively, there needs to be dialogue and discussion between the three parties prior to the signing of the mobility agreement having agreed the common goals which are acceptable.&nbsp;</p>                      </div>

        <h2 class="eche-report-section-title eche-pdf-page-break">During the mobility</h2>
        <div class="eche-report-section-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-report-full-question-wrapper">
                <div class="eche-officer-question-title-wrapper">
                    <div class="eche-report-title-icons-wrapper">
                                                 <div class="eche-report-officer-number">
                            <img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/eche-pdf/number-corner-orange-10.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">

                            <div class="eche-report-officer-number-text">10</div>
                        </div>
                        <div class="eche-officer-question-icon"><img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/ECHE__OFFICERS_Q10.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">
</div>
                    </div>
                    <div class="eche-report-title-question-text-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-officer-question"> During the mobility, your institution fosters the integration of the incoming mobile participants</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The institution appoints responsible person(s) to deal with practical issues (e.g. social, health, and/or psychological problems)</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The institution should ensure there are named, visible persons who are responsible for the practical issues associated with integrating mobile students. This visibility should be ensured through introduction to this function during the Welcome / Orientation period and be detailed on the website so all mobile students can easily access this support, throughout their stay.&nbsp;</p><p>Non-academic mentoring and support arrangements should already be outlined in the Course Catalogue of the receiving HEI, in the section on general information for students, with relevant contact persons in the respective areas. Academic advisors should have close contact with the practical services which are available to incoming participants as they are often the first line of contact to the incoming student. Further information sessions should be arranged for all staff who work with incoming students to ensure they are adequately signposted on to the appropriate services they require.</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">It appoints responsible person(s) to deal with academic issues (course timetables, student attendance, coursework, relationship with academic staff, etc.)</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>It is important that the receiving institution appoints specific named academic advisors who are responsible for dealing with problems related to academic issues (course timetables, student attendance, coursework, relationship with academic staff, etc.) of incoming students.&nbsp; Information on mentoring for thesis writing for incoming students is particularly important and clear mentoring arrangements should be agreed upon between the student, sending and receiving institutions and organised before the mobility.</p><p>For traineeships, a mentor, different from the supervisor, should be nominated to support and encourage the mobile student while in the receiving organisation. The mentor should also provide information on the culture of the enterprise and informal codes and conducts, of the receiving organisation. The contact details of both the supervisor and the mentor should be specified in the Learning Agreement.</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">It organises Welcome / Orientation activities at the beginning of each semester</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>An important aspect of the support arrangement is the welcome or orientation activities. These welcome / orientation activities should provide the incoming students with the necessary information on practical and administrative arrangements, to allow incoming students to meet local and other mobile students, to introduce the learning and teaching methods of the receiving institution, academic regulations, the institutional culture, health and safety issues. These activities should address any type of concern of the incoming student, and reduce any psychological pressure they might feel during their first contacts at the receiving institution. The welcome&nbsp; / orientation activities should be designed to take into account any cultural and religious sensitivities of the incoming students (ensuring a range of activities to suit different types of students).</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">It organises activities to integrate them in the receiving institution and the local community, e.g. with the support of student organisations, Erasmus+ Student and Alumni Association etc.</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>As well as academic and practical support from the institution, incoming students need to feel fully integrated into the student community, something which is best done by their fellow students / peers. Local student association(s), such as Erasmus Student Network (ESN) and the other associations’ member of the ESAA - Erasmus+ Student and Alumni Association (<a href="http://esaa-eu.org/">http://esaa-eu.org/</a>), play an important role in supporting incoming students. Incoming students need to feel welcomed and included in the student organisations. To help this process, the student organisations need to be aware of their role in supporting this integration and have access to the right resources, information, guidance and incentives. As institutions often have many types of student organisations, cooperation between them is encouraged through meetings together, social activities and buddy programmes. A key aspect of these activities is to make sure they are for all students so incoming students are integrated with the local students and hence the culture. Student organisations include for example, ESN (Erasmus Student Network) or ESAA - Erasmus+ Student and Alumni Association (<a href="http://esaa-eu.org/">http://esaa-eu.org/</a>). ESAA runs a buddy system to encourage integration of incoming students with their peers inside the institution and share good practice with other member associations around Europe.</p>                      </div>

        <h2 class="eche-report-section-title eche-pdf-page-break">After the mobility</h2>
        <div class="eche-report-section-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-report-full-question-wrapper">
                <div class="eche-officer-question-title-wrapper">
                    <div class="eche-report-title-icons-wrapper">
                                                 <div class="eche-report-officer-number">
                            <img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/eche-pdf/number-corner-orange-11.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">

                            <div class="eche-report-officer-number-text">11</div>
                        </div>
                        <div class="eche-officer-question-icon"><img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/ECHE__OFFICERS_Q11.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">
</div>
                    </div>
                    <div class="eche-report-title-question-text-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-officer-question"> At the end of the mobility, your institution has formal procedures for recognising student mobility (good practices linked to recognition at the end of the mobility, e.g. in the use of Transcripts of Records and Grade Distribution Tables)</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Transcripts of Records are issued in a timely manner (normally 5 weeks) to both incoming and outgoing students</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>It is highly important in the recognition framework to provide Transcripts of Records in a timely manner, immediately following the mobility period. After the mobility, the receiving institution should send a Transcript of Records to the student and to the sending institution within a period stipulated in the Inter-Institutional Agreement (normally within five weeks after publication/proclamation of the student’s results at the receiving institution). It can be provided electronically or through any other means accessible to the student and the sending institution. The Transcript of Records from the receiving institution should refer to the educational components agreed upon in the Learning Agreement. Grade distribution information should be included as well, either as a web link or an annex.</p><p>Following the receipt of the Transcript of Records from the receiving institution, the sending institution should automatically transfer and recognise the student’s academic outcomes successfully completed at the receiving institution, as agreed in the Learning Agreement, without the need for the student to take any further courses or exams. The Sending Institution will provide a Transcript of Records to the student or record the results in a database or any other means accessible to the student, normally within five weeks after having received the transcript of the receiving institution. The EU official template for the Learning Agreement for studies (including the Transcript of Records) is available online: <a href="http://ec.europa.eu/education/opportunities/higher-education/quality-framework_en.htm">http://ec.europa.eu/education/opportunities/higher-education/quality-framework_en.htm</a></p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">All credits gained by students during a period of study abroad that were specified in the final version of the Learning Agreement are automatically transferred by your institution and count towards the students' final degree, without the need for the student to take any further courses or exams</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The sending institution should ensure that all the credits earned by the mobile student during the mobility period are recognised and counted towards the final degree, without the need for the student to take any further courses or exams. The period of study abroad must be clear in the student's records and documents issued to the student (Diploma Supplement or equivalent). This is a golden rule of recognition of credit mobility within the framework of inter-institutional agreements. All the credits towards the student's degree that are earned during the mobility period and which were originally agreed on in the Learning Agreement (or a revised version to it) should be recognised by the sending HEI without the need for the student to take any further courses or exams. Learning Agreements are binding for all the parties and require that, on successful completion of the mobility period, the sending HEI recognises credits earned by the student and documents these credits in the student records, so they can be identified in a transparent way.</p><p>Upon receipt of the Transcript of Records or Training Certificates, the sending HEI should:<br>a) certify the mobile student has fulfilled all requirements stipulated in the Learning Agreement;<br>b) ensure recognition of the mobility period abroad within the time-scale and according to the conditions stipulated in the institutional recognition framework.</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Transcripts of Records of incoming students include a description of or a link to the national grading system</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The Transcript of Records from the receiving institution should include grade distribution information, either as a web link or an annex. The local grading scale should be clearly explained, with a statistical distribution of local grades, to provide transparency and understanding of grading practices at the host institution. Where applicable, use should be made of a Grade Distribution Table for the programme of study, according to the ECTS Users’ Guide (<a href="http://ec.europa.eu/education/ects/users-guide/index.htm">http://ec.europa.eu/education/ects/users-guide/index.htm</a>).</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Grades of outgoing students are converted, if applicable, according to a fair and transparent methodology communicated before the mobility</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Grades of outgoing students are converted, if applicable, according to a fair and transparent methodology communicated before the mobility. There are more details on this in the ECTS Users’ Guide.</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">In addition to recognising formal learning, the institution recognises any non-formal or informal learning acquired during the mobility according to the ECTS Users’ Guide, e.g. by awarding ECTS credits for volunteering</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>During a period of mobility, students often take advantage of other opportunities outside of their required courses. These may include specific activities which can be considered non-formal or informal learning where they have acquired new skills. This could include additional language and cultural courses, extra-curricular activities, setting up a business and volunteer work undertaken by the student in that period or upon return at the receiving institution.</p>                      </div>

                                                <h3>Case studies</h3>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/standing-out-from-the-crowd-supporting-students-through-full-recognition-and-documenting-of-mobility-outcomes" target="_blank">"Standing out from the crowd" - supporting students through full recognition and documenting of mobility outcomes</a></div>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/a-common-approach-to-ects-grade-conversion-ensuring-a-fair-assessment-of-student-performance-after-study-abroad" target="_blank">A common approach to ECTS grade conversion, ensuring a fair assessment of student performance after study abroad</a></div>
                                             </div>

                </div>
            </div>

                <div class="eche-officer-question-title-wrapper">
                    <div class="eche-report-title-icons-wrapper">
                                                 <div class="eche-report-officer-number">
                            <img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/eche-pdf/number-corner-orange-12.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">

                            <div class="eche-report-officer-number-text">12</div>
                        </div>
                        <div class="eche-officer-question-icon"><img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/ECHE__OFFICERS_Q12.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">
</div>

                    <div class="eche-report-title-question-text-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-officer-question"> Your institution issues a Diploma Supplement</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">To all students, automatically, free of charge and in a major European language</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>This Supplement should include a record of the period of mobility under the Erasmus+ Programme. The 48 European countries taking part in the Bologna Process have agreed that each mobile graduate in their respective country should receive the Diploma Supplement (DS) automatically, free of charge and in at least one of the major European languages in addition to the national language. The HEI should issue a Diploma Supplement (or equivalent) to accompany every degree successfully completed by a student, using - where applicable - the template developed by the European Commission, the Council of Europe and UNESCO. The HEI's policy on issuing the Diploma Supplement should be published on its website.</p><p>The template for the Diploma Supplement is available at:<br><a href="http://ec.europa.eu/education/tools/diploma-supplement_en.htm">http://ec.europa.eu/education/tools/diploma-supplement_en.htm&nbsp;</a></p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">That includes a record of the mobility period(s) carried out by the student under the Erasmus+ programme</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The information contained in the Transcript of Records from the Receiving Institution should also be included in the Diploma Supplement produced by the Sending Institution (at least for Sending Institutions located in Programme Countries), with the exact titles of the components that the student has followed abroad. Alongside modules or units taken at the sending HEI, the Diploma Supplement should list recognised modules, units and/or training activities undertaken during the student's mobility period and indicate the location of these mobility activities.<br>In the case of double, multiple or joint degrees, the Diploma Supplement should indicate the name and status of the partner HEIs awarding the degree and explain the respective language(s) of instruction and examination. In addition, an explanation should be provided about the grading and classification scheme agreed by the awarding HEIs. The template for the Diploma Supplement is available at:<br><a href="http://ec.europa.eu/education/tools/diploma-supplement_en.htm">http://ec.europa.eu/education/tools/diploma-supplement_en.htm</a>&nbsp;</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-case">
                                                <h3>Case studies</h3>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/the-diploma-supplement-a-tool-to-promote-international-recognition-and-transparency-of-academic-achievement" target="_blank">The Diploma Supplement – a tool to promote international recognition and transparency of academic achievement</a></div>
                                             </div>
                    <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close-text"><i class="fa fa-times fa-2x"></i><span>Close</span></div>
                </div>

                         <div class="eche-report-full-question-wrapper">
                <div class="eche-officer-question-title-wrapper">
                    <div class="eche-report-title-icons-wrapper">
                                                 <div class="eche-report-officer-number">
                            <img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/eche-pdf/number-corner-orange-13.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">

                            <div class="eche-report-officer-number-text">13</div>
                        </div>
                        <div class="eche-officer-question-icon"><img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/ECHE__OFFICERS_Q13.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">
</div>
                    </div>
                    <div class="eche-report-title-question-text-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-officer-question"> Your institution promotes and recognises staff mobility</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By taking it into account in the assessment of their professional development </span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Participation in international projects should be seen as an important aspect of the professional development of the staff and of the modernisation of the HEI and should, therefore, be considered a key component in staff evaluation practices.</p><p>The HEI should link its HR strategy to the objectives set out the internationalisation strategy for staff. For all staff who undertake a period of mobility, HR should be informed and provide support to ensure the identification of the professional development needs of the individual as well as setting out agreed career objectives for their period of mobility. This can be through prepared addendums to staff contracts or through less formal mechanisms of agreed objectives. The new objectives should become part of the normal system of staff evaluation or appraisal and be used in order to recognise the achievements of the staff during the period of mobility. This means that HR staff should be trained to ensure these additional objectives are formally evidenced and recorded in staff records and lead to other rewards and recognition.&nbsp;</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Through, for example the reduction of the teaching load, promotion or pay rises</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>It is highly important to incentivise staff to participate in mobility activities. In order to support and encourage mobility, HEIs should provide a number of incentives to ensure that when staff return to the sending institution, they have long term career benefits. HEIs should acknowledge periods of mobility as a normal part of a career path. Staff working schedules and agreed objectives (in terms of research outputs and assessments) should be adapted to meet their new requirements. Temporary replacements should be found during the mobility period, where possible, to ensure continuity during the mobility period. Upon returning to the sending institution, incentives to maintain links with other institutions or networks should be put in place through providing the time to nurture new relationships (reduction in teaching or research loads, continued related objectives set in performance appraisals). The new objectives set with HR for the period of mobility should be ones which are explicitly recognised and rewarded through promotion, awards or pay rises. Additional cultural / language skills should be recognised as a component in any evaluation / assessment of the staff. This may be achieved by making it well-known that participation is a formal part of staff evaluation procedures, and may lead to improvements in both working conditions and promotion or broader career prospects.</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By encouraging them to propose improvements to the institutional strategy for internationalisation and overarching structure, as well as for structural reform</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>One important form of recognition for staff, which is equally beneficial to the HEI is to encourage their involvement in improving internationalisation and structural reform within the institution. This includes the opportunity for staff to provide feedback into the management structures of departments and the overall institution. There should be a firm commitment - perhaps in writing - from the HEI to recognise and make use of constructive feedback as well as the appropriate forums for staff to engage with senior management to discuss their experiences and propose new ideas for improvement.&nbsp;</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By inviting them to share new learning and teaching practices developed abroad with their peers in the institution</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The experience of staff should be valued and shared as an inspiration to others, by, for example, organising meetings and publishing articles where the mobile participants share their experience and the impact of mobility on their personal and professional development. Where staff are involved in teaching at host institutions, new learning and teaching practices can be brought back and shared with other staff members through seminars or presentations. Staff can be supported through the administrative and academic services to understand the skills they have acquired and how best to use them within their own institution.</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By encouraging them to propose cooperation projects with their receiving organisation</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Mobile staff bring back new partners, networks and ideas which can be of significant value for the HEI. Staff should be encouraged to propose and develop new or further cooperation projects between their receiving and sending institutions. This requires time and commitment, which need to be given formally by the sending institution, including, for example, additional support to write joint proposals.&nbsp;</p>                      </div>

                         <div class="eche-report-full-question-wrapper">
                <div class="eche-officer-question-title-wrapper">
                    <div class="eche-report-title-icons-wrapper">
                                                 <div class="eche-report-officer-number">
                            <img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/eche-pdf/number-corner-orange-14.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">

                            <div class="eche-report-officer-number-text">14</div>
                        </div>
                        <div class="eche-officer-question-icon"><img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/ECHE__OFFICERS_Q14.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">
</div>
                    </div>
                    <div class="eche-report-title-question-text-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-officer-question"> With regards to the outcomes and experiences of Erasmus+ activities</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The results are monitored, evaluated and disseminated as a way to improve international cooperation and mobility activities</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Linked with the overall internationalisation strategy of the institution, monitoring and evaluation of cooperation projects and Erasmus+ mobility is essential if HEIs are to learn from their experiences. Monitoring and evaluation is more than just measuring the number and types of outputs, it needs to include capturing information on the overall outcomes and experiences of the activities at the institutional and the individual level. Systematic monitoring and evaluation should therefore include more qualitative approaches, which expressly capture the experiences in a way which helps the institution to understand the added value of its involvement in these activities. Documenting and analysing the outcomes and experiences is only the first step. To learn from the approaches taken, and the benefits gained, institutions should take time to disseminate the findings of the cooperation projects and mobility periods through, for example, meetings, workshops and publications, social media, etc. These activities will embed good practice, help the institution to iteratively improve its approach and also feed back into the on-going monitoring and evaluation.</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The results are used systematically for the benefit of your institution, providing internationalisation at home, hence enhancing intercultural competences of non-mobile students and staff</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The outcomes and experiences of cooperation and Erasmus+ mobility have a much wider impact than just improving mobile activities. All institutions have significant numbers of non-mobile staff and students who can benefit from the international experiences of others. As part of the monitoring and evaluation processes, HEIs should consider the impact which can be specifically made on non-mobile staff and students, giving them “internationalisation at home experiences”. This includes building international competences, cultural awareness, virtual mobility opportunities, inviting international lecturers and embedding student projects with an international focus into the curricula, and providing opportunities for local students to work together with incoming mobile participants in e.g. project work, to ensure that local students benefit from the presence of mobile students at their institution. This fits with the activities of disseminating the overall outcomes and experiences of the cooperation projects and Erasmus+ mobility, though tailored to a different audience. It should take into account the professional development needs of the staff at the HEI and the perspectives of non-mobile students.&nbsp;</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The results are exploited and disseminated, by providing participants with the results of cooperation projects and Erasmus+ mobility opportunities (e.g. presentations) to share funding possibilities</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The dissemination of outcomes is an integral part of mobility projects. Good practice would be to ensure that the dissemination is built into the support measure and participants in projects and mobility actions are allocated adequate time, resources and space to disseminate their experiences and exploit project results. This includes opportunities to share new knowledge and to highlight new opportunities (including funding) which have arisen from the new relationships formed. In order to do this, HEIs should provide support functions such as web platforms to collect results or opportunities to present results at the institutional or departmental level, as relevant.&nbsp;</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">After the mobility Erasmus+ participants have the opportunity to present their newly acquired competences</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The study entitled ‘Effects of mobility on the skills and employability of students and the internationalisation of higher education institutions’ showcases how mobility can contribute to the internationalisation of higher education institutions, including the impacts on teaching methods, cooperation between HEIs and perception of staff more generally. Therefore the dissemination of outcomes is an integral part of mobility projects. Good practice would be to ensure that the dissemination is built into the support measure and participants in projects and mobility actions are allocated adequate time, resources and space to disseminate their experiences and exploit project results. This includes opportunities to share new knowledge and to highlight new opportunities (including funding) which have arisen from the new relationships formed. In order to do this, HEIs should provide support functions such as web platforms to collect results or opportunities to present results at the institutional or departmental level, as relevant.&nbsp;</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-case">
                                                <h3>Case studies</h3>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/capitalising-on-the-outcomes-and-experiences-of-erasmus-activities" target="_blank">Capitalising on the outcomes and experiences of Erasmus+ activities</a></div>

                    About the Role at RobCo<\/strong><\/p>

                    RobCo is building the category of Autonomous Industrial Robotics and we're doing it fast. We believe that automating the ordinary frees humans to do the extraordinary, and we're building the end-to-end robotics infrastructure to make that possible - hardware, software, and AI in one stack that just works. <\/p>

                    \u00a0<\/div>

                    At RobCo, we automate the ordinary, so humans can do the extraordinary. To achieve this, we are looking for an ambitious Manager Robotic Sales Engineering (m\/f\/d) to help us establish RobCo as leading provider of automation solutions.<\/p>

                    Your mission<\/strong><\/p>

                    Robotic Sales Engineers (RSEs) are RobCo\u2019s technical face to the customer. They qualify opportunities, run requirement workshops, check feasibility and drive each deal to a concept our Solutions Development team can build.<\/p>

                    As Manager Robotic Sales Engineering, you lead a team of around six RSEs and report to the Head of Robotic Sales Engineering. You make sure every deal gets the right technical lead, every customer gets a consistent experience and every RSE on your team keeps getting better. You carry a quota together with Sales and are measured on whether your team hits it.<\/p>

                    You are a player-coach. You lead the team, and you still go on-site for the deals that matter most. You work where modular robotics, software and AI come together, and you help scale how RobCo brings physical AI into real production.<\/p>

                    What you will do<\/strong><\/p>

                    • Lead and grow the team<\/strong> \u2013 Hire, onboard and coach your RSEs. Run regular 1:1s, give clear feedback, write performance reviews and build real career paths.<\/p><\/li>

                    • Deliver the quota<\/strong> \u2013 Own your team\u2019s quota together with your Sales counterparts. Track pipeline and win rates, spot deals at risk early and put your team\u2019s capacity where it moves the number.<\/p><\/li>

                    • Raise the quality bar<\/strong> \u2013 Set the standard for discovery, requirement workshops, feasibility checks and handovers. Review the critical concepts before they go to the customer or to Solutions Development.<\/p><\/li>

                    • Be hands-on where it counts<\/strong> \u2013 Join strategic accounts and complex workshops yourself, and be the technical escalation point for customers and AEs.<\/p><\/li>

                    • Own the interfaces<\/strong> \u2013 Work closely with Sales leadership, Solutions Development and Product to keep handovers clean and expectations aligned.<\/p><\/li>

                    • Improve how we work<\/strong> \u2013 Shape the team\u2019s processes, templates, tools and KPIs, and turn field insights into input for Product.<\/p><\/li><\/ul>

Company Description

Swish Analytics is a sports analytics, betting and fantasy startup building the next generation of predictive sports analytics data products. We're looking for team-oriented individuals with an authentic passion for accurate and predictive real-time data who can execute in a fast-paced, creative, and continually-evolving environment without sacrificing technical excellence.   • Production experience with Kafka or comparable stream-processing systems

We are seeking an experienced Senior iOS App Developer with an excellent background in native iOS development using Swift and SwiftUI, together with practical experience integrating Kotlin Multiplatform into iOS applications.

This is a hands-on engineering role. You will develop and improve our iOS application, integrate shared application logic, solve complex technical problems, and establish effective workflows for AI-assisted and agentic development.

  • Develop, maintain, and improve our native iOS application using Swift and SwiftUI.
  • Integrate Kotlin Multiplatform modules into the iOS application and collaborate on shared business logic.

Job Description:

We are GDIT. We stay at the forefront of innovation to solve complex technical challenges.

GDIT is your place. Make it your own by discovering new ways to apply the latest technology and processes. Own your opportunity at GDIT and you’ll be a meaningful part of improving how agencies operate. Our work depends on a Committee Operations Lead joining our team to lead IT professionals supporting the Health Resources & Services Administration (HRSA).

The Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA) aims to improve health outcomes by enhancing access to quality services, developing a skilled health workforce, and implementing innovative programs that benefit geographically isolated, economically or medically vulnerable populations. HRSA focuses on increasing health equity and strengthening local health systems through initiatives such as community health centers, the Organ Procurement & Transplantation Network (OPTN), the Ryan White HIV/AIDS Program, and support for maternal and child health.

At GDIT, we foster a people-centric environment. The Committee Operations Lead will manage and facilitate the activities of Organ Procurement and Transplantation Network (OPTN) committees, including subcommittees, workgroups, and ad hoc groups. This role ensures that committees responsible for membership, patient safety, and policy development operate efficiently, transparently, and in alignment with statutory, regulatory, and policy-driven goals.

The Committee Operations Lead functions as a pivotal project manager, policy facilitator, and liaison, supporting committees in their critical decision-making, managing governance documentation, streamlining meeting logistics, and collaborating with internal and external stakeholders. They also support the development and implementation of evidence-based transplantation and allocation policies, ensuring compliance with HRSA and federal regulations.

This role combines project management expertise, policy analysis skills, and regulatory knowledge to deliver high-quality support to committee operations and optimize system performance. In this role, the responsibilities of the Committee Operations Lead will include:

  • Lead and support OPTN committees tasked with membership oversight, patient safety, and policy development.

  • Oversee the schedule and facilitation of committee meetings, develop detailed agendas, prepare support materials, and lead discussions in a manner promoting collaboration and timely decision-making.

  • Collaborate with committee chairs and leadership to ensure accurate tracking of activities, timely communication, and seamless facilitation of committee initiatives.

  • Fully implement a Committee(s) Meeting Facilitation Plan that ensures secure, efficient, and compliant virtual meetings, including maintaining schedules, technical support, and post-meeting documentation (recordings, minutes, summaries).

  • Develop, implement, and maintain the Committee(s) Management Plan, which outlines procedures for tracking committee activities, milestones, composition, and outputs.

  • Create and maintain governance documents, operational manuals, and SOPs related to committee structures, member selection processes, decision-making responsibilities, and conflict-of-interest logs.

  • Prepare public-facing materials highlighting committee activities, accomplishments, and membership, ensuring transparency and alignment with organizational goals.

  • Support policy development by identifying opportunities to improve organ transplantation and allocation policies through evidence-based research and committee-led initiatives.

  • Draft policy proposals, guidance documents, public comment reports, and board recommendations based on committee deliberations and feedback.

  • Collaborate with OPTN committees and stakeholders to ensure all proposed policies align with federal regulations (e.g., CMS, HRSA). Maintain thorough documentation for policy audits and regulatory reporting.

  • Analyze quantitative and qualitative data (using tools such as Excel, Tableau, or NVivo) to support committee decision-making and policy recommendations.

  • Provide detailed reports and dashboards on committee outputs, performance trends, and policy impact to OPTN leadership, HRSA, and other stakeholders.

  • Track and monitor committee projects and policy proposals through all stages (inception to implementation), ensuring alignment with public comment periods and board approval timelines.

  • Act as the primary point of contact for committee members and stakeholders, facilitating communication, responding to inquiries, and resolving operational challenges.

  • Engage with the broader transplant community to gather input, understand concerns, and encourage collaboration in policy discussions and system improvements.

  • Collaborate with external contractors, OPTN support teams, and other divisions, such as IT and policy experts, to facilitate seamless coordination across all committee activities.

  • Lead the development of the Committee(s) Training Plan, which provides onboarding, annual training, and up-to-date resources for committee members.

  • Ensure training materials address committee structures, workflows, regulatory requirements, and membership expectations.

  • Deliver virtual training sessions and maintain a secure repository of training recordings and resources.

  • Implement the Subject Matter Expertise Plan to identify, onboard, and track expert contributors across clinical, analytical, policy, and risk management domains.

  • Ensure timely and sustained access to experts who support committee initiatives related to membership evaluation, patient safety reviews, and policy recommendations.

WHAT YOU'LL NEED

  • Bachelor’s degree in Public Health, Public Policy, Health Administration, Business Administration, or a related field. Master’s degree (MPH, MPP, MHA) is preferred.

  • At least 5+ years of experience in committee coordination, project management, or policy development.

  • Experience in healthcare, compliance, regulatory, and/or nonprofit environments, especially in roles requiring meeting facilitation and multi-stakeholder engagement.

  • Proven ability to lead virtual committee meetings, guide collaborative decision-making, and manage cross-functional initiatives.

  • Strong understanding of policy drafting, federal regulations, and evidence-based research to inform recommendations and decisions.

  • Proficiency in quantitative and qualitative data analysis, with tools such as Tableau, NVivo, and Excel.

  • Familiarity with healthcare regulations (e.g., CMS, HRSA) and experience ensuring policies meet federal and organizational requirements.

  • Exceptional written and verbal communication abilities, with a focus on preparing detailed reports, agendas, and governance materials.

  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (SharePoint, Teams), virtual meeting platforms, and committee documentation systems.

  • Excellent attention to detail, time management, and multitasking in fast-paced, deadline-driven environments.

  • Must be able to obtain a Public Trust clearance

Lumen is the trusted network for the AI‑powered world, connecting people, data, and applications through our expansive fiber network and connected ecosystem. We enable secure, high‑performance connectivity across cloud, edge, and AI workloads for enterprises, governments, and communities.

At Lumen, you’ll work on infrastructure customers rely on today and build for what’s next, where performance, security, and resilience matter.

This is a high accountability environment where bold ideas drive real innovation for our customers, partners, and industry. The work is challenging, expectations are clear, and trust is built into how we operate. If you’re ready to take ownership, deliver meaningful impact, and help shape the future of AI‑ready connectivity, join us today.

The Role

The Lead Product Manager – Ethernet Network owns the strategy, roadmap, delivery, go-to-market execution, and lifecycle performance of Lumen’s Ethernet network product. This role serves as the accountable business voice for the product within its Agile Release Train (ART), translating customer needs, market opportunities, product-line priorities, and network strategy into a clear, prioritized feature backlog that engineering teams can execute. The Lead Product Manager partners across architecture, engineering, operations, sales, marketing, finance, legal, and regulatory teams to evolve the Ethernet network, improve customer outcomes, and deliver sustainable revenue and margin growth. The role requires strong technical and commercial judgment, disciplined product leadership, and hands-on Agile Product Manager accountability within Lumen’s SAFe operating model.

The Main Responsibilities

  • Own the Ethernet network product vision, strategy, roadmap, objectives, and key results across the full lifecycle—from concept and investment through launch, growth, optimization, and retirement.
  • Act as the voice of the customer by analyzing customer needs, market trends, competitive alternatives, sales insights, and operational data to define differentiated product capabilities and priorities.
  • Develop and maintain a 12–24 month product roadmap aligned with Lumen’s network evolution, business strategy, transformation priorities, and related product portfolios.
  • Own, maintain, and prioritize the product’s feature backlog, ensuring features have clear business outcomes, requirements, acceptance criteria, dependencies, and readiness for engineering execution.
  • Write and prioritize features in close partnership with Product Owners, System Architects, engineering teams, and other delivery partners; decompose higher-level capabilities and strategic direction into executable increments of value.
  • Represent the product in SAFe planning and delivery activities, including PI Planning, roadmap and vision reviews, backlog refinement, PO Sync, System Demos, and outcome reviews.
  • Track and manage product-level risks, assumptions, dependencies, impediments, and trade-offs in Jira, escalating decisions that require broader product-line or leadership alignment.
  • Partner with Technical Program Managers and delivery leaders to coordinate cross-team dependencies and maintain transparency on scope, sequencing, milestones, and delivery health.
  • Lead product-level business planning, including business cases, pricing inputs, investment and resource needs, revenue and margin opportunities, and ongoing measurement of ROI, KPIs, OKRs, and backlog health.
  • Coordinate go-to-market and launch readiness across engineering, network operations, marketing, sales, customer success, support, finance, legal, and regulatory stakeholders.
  • Enable sales and solution teams with clear positioning, customer benefits, competitive differentiation, roadmap guidance, and assessment of qualified feature or customization requests.
  • Maintain accurate, current product documentation and communications, and provide clear updates on strategy, roadmap, delivery progress, product performance, and decisions.
  • Build subject-matter expertise in Ethernet services, network capabilities, customer use cases, and the applicable competitive and regulatory environment.
  • Influence and align cross-functional teams without direct authority, using data, customer insight, and sound product judgment to drive decisions and accountability.

What We Look For in a Candidate

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent education and relevant experience.
  • Five or more years of experience in product management, technical product ownership, or a related discipline within telecommunications, networking, software, platform, or technology services.
  • Demonstrated end-to-end ownership of a product or major feature area, including strategy, roadmap development, requirements, delivery, launch, and performance management.
  • Experience translating customer and business needs into well-defined features, requirements, and acceptance criteria in partnership with engineering teams.
  • Working knowledge of Ethernet services and network technologies, with the technical aptitude to evaluate product, platform, API, operational, and architectural trade-offs.
  • Experience operating in an Agile or SAFe delivery environment, including backlog prioritization, PI Planning, and cross-functional delivery coordination.
  • Demonstrated ability to use customer insight, market analysis, financial data, and performance metrics to make product investment and prioritization decisions.
  • Experience developing business cases and supporting pricing, go-to-market, launch-readiness, and sales-enablement activities.
  • Strong written, verbal, presentation, and stakeholder-management skills, with the ability to communicate effectively with technical teams, business partners, and senior leaders.
  • Proven ability to lead through influence, manage competing priorities, resolve ambiguity, and deliver results in a fast-paced matrixed organization.
  • Hands-on proficiency with Jira and Microsoft Excel; familiarity with APIs, product analytics, and roadmap or portfolio-management tools is preferred.

Location

Our Scaled Account Manager will be an integral part of DoiT’s Account Management organization in AMER. This role is remote and open to candidates located in North America.

Who We Are
DoiT is a global technology company that works with cloud-driven organizations to leverage the cloud to drive business growth and innovation. We combine data, technology, and human expertise to ensure our customers operate in a well-architected and scalable state - from planning to production.

Delivering DoiT Cloud Intelligence, the only solution that integrates advanced technology with human intelligence, we help our customers solve complex multicloud problems and drive efficiency.

With decades of multicloud experience, we have specializations in Kubernetes, GenAI, CloudOps, and more. An award-winning strategic partner of AWS, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure, we work alongside more than 4,000 customers worldwide.

The Opportunity
DoiT’s Account Management team is responsible for retaining and growing our existing customer base by building trusted relationships, identifying high-value opportunities for deeper engagement, and serving as a strategic point of contact for cloud-provider teams supporting customer growth. The team’s goal is to protect 100% of existing business while identifying customers with the strongest potential for expansion, advocacy, and long-term partnership.

As a Scaled Account Manager, you will own the commercial relationship and customer strategy across a large portfolio of primarily SMB and mid-market accounts. You will use an efficient, repeatable coverage model to identify and prioritize customers who are scaling quickly, developing larger cloud and technology footprints, or showing a need for deeper technical engagement. You will focus your time where DoiT can create the greatest impact—whether that means expanding the current relationship, integrating additional cloud or technology environments not yet managed through DoiT, or introducing standalone DoiT products that address clear customer needs.

You will act as the business lead for your portfolio, combining account insight, commercial judgment, and customer discovery to uncover qualified growth opportunities. You will partner closely with Customer Success Managers, Forward Deployed Engineers, DoiT specialists, and cloud-provider teams to understand customers’ evolving environments, align DoiT’s expertise and products to their priorities, and help them make better decisions about their cloud strategy.

Success means protecting the existing business, identifying high-growth customers early, increasing adoption of DoiT’s products and expertise, expanding DoiT’s role across customers’ broader technology footprints, and creating durable commercial growth through both integrated services and standalone product placement.

Responsibilities

  • Own a scaled portfolio primarily in the SMB and mid-market segments, using Salesforce to maintain customer context, stakeholders, priorities, risks, opportunities, renewals, and next steps.
  • Use data to prioritize engagement across the portfolio, focusing on high-potential and at-risk accounts; build multi-threaded relationships and understand each customer’s business priorities, cloud footprint, FinOps maturity, and desired outcomes.
  • Drive retention and renewal outcomes by identifying risk early, coordinating mitigation plans, and leading commercial conversations with internal partners on pricing, commitments, contracts, and approvals.
  • Identify, qualify, and manage expansion pipeline across new workloads, migrations, cost optimization, managed commitments, DoiT products, and services; maintain accurate opportunity stages and forecasts.
  • Partner with Sales, CSMs, FDEs, DoiT specialists, and cloud-provider teams on account plans, funding, deal registration, and execution, delegating delivery work while owning the commercial relationship.
  • Run portfolio-appropriate customer cadences, including account and FinOps reviews, product demonstrations, commitment planning, security and AI discussions, onboarding, and escalation reviews.
  • Coordinate escalations to the right DoiT owner, keeping customers informed and driving accountability through resolution.
  • Use customer data, dashboards, CRM workflows, and appropriate AI or automation tools to improve coverage and create repeatable operating rhythms.
  • Capture and share actionable customer feedback, product requests, and market insights with Product, Engineering, Marketing, and Sales.
  • Maintain account reviews and plans for priority and high-potential customers, tracking outcomes, engagement, spend trends, risks, renewal timing, and growth plans.

Qualifications

  • 2+ years of experience in an Account Management/Customer Success/Customer Engineering role
  • 3+ years of experience in a technology company
  • Strong verbal/written communication skills in English
  • Strong technical skills that enable you to engage productively with technical teams and the ability to build influential relationships
  • Great operational/administration skills, analytical, detail-oriented and able to “zoom” in/out from the big picture to the minutiae
  • A desire to grow within the organization and continuously broaden your skill sets
  • A great sense of humor and enjoys having fun at work

Bonus Points

  • Experience with AWS, GCP, or other major public clouds
  • Experience with FinOps, cloud cost optimization, cloud operations, Kubernetes, AI, data platforms, or related cloud technologies.
  • Cloud Certifications (AWS cloud practitioner or Google Cloud Digital Leader certifications)

Help train and evaluate AI agents that work inside a real CAD environment on long engineering tasks, work that would take an expert 10–15 hours.   • 5+ years of professional, hands-on CAD modelling (CATIA, SolidWorks, Siemens NX, Creo or similar). Experience preparing geometry for simulation (ANSYS or similar) is a strong plus.

  • Comfortable with Python and GitHub.

Project time expectations

For this project, tasks are estimated to require around 10–20 hours per week during active phases, based on project requirements. This is an estimate, not a guaranteed workload, and applies only while the project is active.

About Tastemade

Tastemade, part of Wonder, brings together a community of people to discover mouth-watering cuisines from around the world, explore never-before-seen destinations, and elevate everyday living spaces.

We create award-winning video content and original programming in the categories of Food, Travel, and Home & Design across all major streaming and social platforms, making it easy for our global audience of millions of monthly viewers to tune in and enjoy.

Tastemade has been recognized with more than 65 awards, including three Emmy® Awards, three James Beard Awards, numerous Webby Awards, and has been twice recognized as one of Fast Company’s “Most Innovative Companies." This is where taste is made.

Join the Tastemade team—the ultimate lifestyle video storytellers. Inspire viewers to try new recipes in their own kitchen and embark on unforgettable journeys. You’ll help make the everyday more exciting, delicious, and extraordinary.

About The Opportunity


Tastemade is looking for a Social Media Senior Manager to support our mission and be a key role player in developing our broader content strategy across platforms. The ideal candidate will have an extensive background in content creation for social media and/or editorial, a deep understanding of social and YouTube analytics, and proven ability to amplify entertainment and lifestyle brands.


The Impact You Will Make

  • Lead social media for the company and act as an integral part of building strategy that leans into our award winning programming in the food / lifestyle space
  • Lead audience and revenue growth on priority social media platforms by creating and platforming content that resonates with our audience and helps support our broader programming initiatives
  • Manage all aspects of content optimization & packaging across priority social platforms
  • Develop, implement and manage operations that are scalable and efficient, including continuously evaluating and refining processes within Social
  • Closely monitor our Social Content Budget and regularly analyze ROI
  • Develop strategies for emerging platforms, which may include leading the creation of content and posting as needed
  • Stay constantly up to date on social media competitor trends across all platforms

What You Bring to the Table

  • 7-10 years experience in social media, digital video and/or editorial with at least 2 years managing a team or contractors
  • Specific experience managing YouTube channels
  • Expert in social media metrics, analytics and reporting, including experience using YouTube Studio & Analytics
  • Proven ability to engage, connect and build an audience across multiple channels
  • Ability to interpret analytics, form insights and communicate the resulting strategy to both executives and your team
  • Basic knowledge of the Adobe suite (especially Photoshop and Premiere) a plus
  • A passion for Tastemade, all things food, and a positive, get-it-done attitude!
  • Adaptable and able to perform well during periods of change

Got These? Even Better

  • A creative storyteller who understands how to connect with social audiences on all social channels using great copy, video and interactions.
  • An intuitive leader ready to contribute who has excellent communication skills, both written and verbal, and able to lead projects across multiple departments with ease.
  • An investigator who uses data and analysis to determine what tactics are inspiring audiences.
  • An experimenter who is constantly looking for new ways to surprise, delight and inspire viewers.
  • An avid user of all priority platforms, both personally and professionally, including deep experience with YouTube related to strategy and content optimization

Position: Recruitment/ HR Assistant (Full time)

Role Overview:
The HR Coordinator supports the client's HR consultants across several client accounts. Each coordinator works alongside an assigned consultant on day-to-day HR administration for clients in healthcare, behavioral health, nonprofit and multi-unit industries. The role is built for someone who wants to grow their HR skills through hands-on work in different systems, industries and HR functions. Coordinators support client HR work only. They do not handle Corel's internal marketing or social media.

Key Specific Tasks the HR Coordinator Will Do:

  1. Recruiting support: Post jobs, screen applicants, schedule interviews, communicate with candidates and keep applicant tracking up to date.
  2. Reference and pre-employment checks: Run reference checks, start background checks and verify licenses or credentials where a role requires them.
  3. Onboarding coordination: Prepare offer letters and new hire packets, collect I-9s and other onboarding paperwork, set up employees in client HRIS systems and track onboarding checklists to completion.
  4. Offboarding support: Process separation paperwork, keep checklists and records up to date, and update the HRIS.
  5. HR document creation: Draft and format job descriptions, offer letters, policies, forms, templates and employee communications using AI tools and client templates.
  6. SOP writing: Write clear, step-by-step SOPs and process guides for client HR workflows and client's internal processes. Document how tasks are done in each client's HRIS.
  7. HRIS administration and data entry: Keep employee records accurate across client HRIS and payroll platforms. Run reports and check that data matches between systems.
  8. HR audits and spreadsheet work: Run PTO audits, personnel file audits, headcount and roster reconciliations, and compliance tracking.
  9. Inbox management: Manage and triage email for assigned consultants and client HR inboxes. Draft replies, flag priorities and route requests to the right person.
  10. Task and project management: Turn meeting transcripts and consultant notes into action items with AI tools, then create, track and update tasks in Asana so deliverables are met on time.
  11. AI-assisted workflows: Use Claude and other AI tools every day to draft documents, summarize calls, analyze data and streamline repeatable HR tasks.
  12. Internal HR library support: Help build and maintain Corel's HR Q&A library, SOPs and templates.
  13. General HR administration: Handle other HR support tasks as assigned by the consultant.
  14. Ability to Work with a team and respond to requests timely

Software Tools and Websites Required:

  1. HRIS and payroll platforms: Hands-on experience with at least one or two of the platforms below is a plus. Candidates should list the specific platforms they've used and what they did in each, such as onboarding, employee record updates, reporting, PTO tracking or payroll data entry. If they don't have HRIS, a relevant CRM, Project Management or other can be considered as applicable experience.
    • ADP (Workforce Now / Run)
    • Gusto
    • Paylocity
    • Paycom
    • Paychex Flex
    • Rippling
    • BambooHR
    • UKG (Ready / Pro)
    • Paycor
    • Justworks
    • Namely
    • Workday (a plus)
  2. AI tools, especially Claude (strongly preferred), ChatGPT or Gemini: Comfortable using AI for writing, summarizing, data work and process efficiency. This is a core skill for the role.
  3. Google Workspace (Gmail, Meet, Chat, Docs, Sheets, Drive): Proficiency required.
  4. Asana or a similar project management tool (Monday, ClickUp, Trello): Experience required.
  5. Excel and Google Sheets: Strong data management skills required, including formulas, lookups, filtering and data cleanup

Ideal Candidate Qualifications:

  1. 3+ years of HR administration, HR coordinator or HR assistant experience or relevant education and degree in Human Resources.
  2. Hands-on experience in at least one major HRIS, such as ADP, Gusto or Paylocity or similar platform
  3. Proven ability to understand SOPs, process documents or training guides. It is a plus if the candidate can write and create documentation processes.
  4. Understanding of the basic employee lifecycle: recruiting, onboarding, employee records and offboarding
  5. Strong attention to detail when handling confidential employee data
  6. Can manage several clients and priorities at once and communicate clearly with consultants
  7. Eager to learn HR and take on more over time
  8. US-based HR experience is a plus
  9. Excellent written and verbal English and Spanish communication

Software Tools and Websites Willing to train on:

  1. Internal Asana workflows and templates
  2. Client's AI workflows and Claude projects
  3. Client-specific HRIS platforms
  4. Company-specific processes and SOPs
  5. Client-specific HR procedures and compliance requirements

Job Title

Retail Process and Support Coordinator

Job Description

Coordinator, Retail Processes and Support

Location: Remote

Travel: Up to 20% of the time, attending meetings in Washington DC and potential store travel

Who We Are

At Framebridge, we are disrupting the custom framing market by replacing a cumbersome experience with a delightful one. Our mission is to make framing so delightful, customers are inspired to frame everything they love—big, little and in between. We've framed over three million pieces and counting. We are building a beloved brand, and to be successful, we have to build a great team across a number of disciplines – ecommerce, retail, design, and manufacturing.

We are a consumer business operating online and in our growing fleet of retail stores. We operate multiple manufacturing studios that allow us to deliver a high-quality custom product at an affordable price with a quick turnaround. We exist, grow, and ultimately own the market by delighting customers who trust and value us.

The Role

We're seeking a Coordinator, Retail Processes and Support who will play a pivotal role in ensuring the smooth and efficient operation of our retail stores, managing store logistics and supplies, developing documentation and SOPs, and serving as a liaison between corporate teams and store personnel. This role reports to Director, Retail Processes and Operations.

As a Framebridge Team Member, You Will:

Show Pride

We stand behind our work, we sweat the details, and we strive for continuous improvement every day. We're proud to frame the things you love, and show pride in our product and craftsmanship.

Adapt & Act

We are creative and solution-oriented, flexible, and proactive. We adapt and act quickly, embracing an environment of constant change.

Embrace Challenges

We embrace challenges with creative solutions and we know that collaboration is the only way to succeed. We set big goals and keep raising the bar together.

Secure the Baton

We take personal responsibility for delivering successful outcomes, not just completing tasks. We ensure every handoff is clear, complete, and sets the next teammates up to succeed.

Make It Special

We search everyday for opportunities to make our product and experience special. When you are building a business where every piece is priceless, making it special is core.

Build to Last

We are building a product and a business that are built to last. We work every day to build lasting relationships within our team and with our customers.

At Framebridge, our people are the heart of everything we build. We foster an inclusive, equitable, and collaborative environment where remarkable individuals take pride in their craft, elevate the customer experience, and are empowered to do the best work of their careers.

As Coordinator, Retail Processes and Support, You Will:

  • Monitor store and district compliance across a wide range of KPI measures, customer satisfaction, and productivity standards — using data to surface trends, flag risks, and identify opportunities for improvement.
  • Serve as administrator and subject matter expert for store-specific systems, both proprietary and vendor-supported, maintaining a working understanding of how those systems connect and how process changes affect them.
  • Act as liaison between stores and HQ, helping to answer questions and support field team requests that come through direct messages, Slack, email, or surveys.
  • Monitor task and compliance completion, generate reporting (e.g. task completion rates, customer sentiment metrics, payroll reporting, new product launch adoption), and share results with field leadership on a regular cadence.
  • Work closely with factory logistics teams to support store shuttle schedules, supply needs and procurement, and physical inventory movement.
  • Execute internal processes such as store hours updates across platforms, creation of monthly operational trackers, and other recurring workflows.
  • Assist with the creation and upkeep of Store Policies and Procedures.

Who You Are:

  • At least 3+ years of retail experience.
  • Live in a market where you are local to a store location.
  • Analytical and data-driven, with a natural curiosity about the why behind performance trends — you use data to identify opportunities for process improvement and growth, not just to report on what happened.
  • Strong understanding of how systems work and intersect; you think about how process decisions upstream affect outcomes downstream and ask questions to understand those connections.
  • Strong organizational and time-management skills, with the ability to prioritize tasks and meet deadlines in a fast-paced environment.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to effectively engage with diverse stakeholders.
  • Detail-oriented mindset with a focus on accuracy and quality in all tasks.
  • Proficiency in Google Workspace and/or Microsoft Office suite.
  • Ability to adapt to changing priorities and work independently as well as part of a team.

Benefits & Perks:

  • Full medical, dental, and vision benefits
  • Generous retirement program — 401(k) and employer-funded pension plan
  • Parental leave and return program
  • Flexible Time Off and paid holidays
  • Framebridge employee Free Frame codes and discounts
  • Short-term disability and Life/AD&D Insurance
  • Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
  • Ongoing learning and development opportunities
  • Commuter benefits
  • Pet insurance
  • And more!

Salary Information:

The base salary for this role is $70,000. Final compensation depends on experience, qualifications, and location.
